newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Jan manufacturers' shipments rise 2.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Jan manufacturers' shipments rise 2.2 pct.

text.p: Canadian manufacturers' shipments rose 2.2 percent in January, to C$35.05 billion seasonally adjusted from a revised C$34.29 billion (C$34.22 billion) in December, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast shipments to rise 0.9 percent, unfilled orders to rise 0.7 percent, new orders to rise 0.6 percent and an inventory/shipment ratio of 1.32.

Statistics Canada said Canadian manufacturers got off to a strong start in 1997 as demand for cars and trucks in the United States drove up shipments to record levels and a spate of new contracts swelled order books.

Total manufacturing shipments increased 2.2 percent in January to a record level of C$35.1 billion, the agency said. Makers of motor vehicle parts and primary metals were largely behind the January increase.

Shipments of motor vehicles in rose 10.8 percent, probably because of strong demand from U.S. suppliers whose stocks have been depleted by a major inventory correction and who anticipate an increase in consumer spending, Statscan said.
Primary metals rose 6.0 percent, chemical products rose 5.1 percent and food industries roose 1.9 percent, the agency said.
Manufacturers' backlog of unfilled orders, a key determinant of future shipments, reocrded the largest increase in more than two years, rising 3.0 percent to C$34.8 billion, Statscan said.
January's result is significant because unfilled orders were mainly flat in 1996, the agency said.
